_comment: Robot layout for v4_s1_v4_ll (COOHAVIOR's S1-V4-LL), ported to Merom_1_int.
Positions and scales are both the V4 staging scene's own, from its M5 robot
set. They transfer unchanged because the two coordinate frames are the same
one: of eight BEHAVIOR objects the V4 scene edits, five sit at identical
coordinates in Merom_1_int_best.json, and the three that differ are the
moves that layout makes deliberately.
The scales are not decoration. V4 stages these three within half a metre of
each other, which only fits because it shrinks them -- Ridgeback to 0.5,
Jackal to 0.7, Crazyflie 0.6 (now 2.0, see below). Loaded at full size, two of them overlap,
place_robots relocates them by 0.8 m and 1.9 m, and the relocation shoves
the task's packing box 1.4 m across the room. Size is part of a layout.
The three models are deliberately unequal, which is the point of the task:
only the Ridgeback's UR5 and the Crazyflie's belly suction cup can grasp.
The Jackal has no arm at all -- navigate_to and wait, nothing more -- and V4
uses it as a carrier, a role this action set has no word for yet.
agent_0 is base-locked while holding, which is what V4 states on its own
Ridgeback prim (v4:base_locked_while_holding). It can pick the box up but
not carry it anywhere, so the only route to the bedroom is through agent_1:
agent_0  grasp(box) -> load_onto(agent_1)
agent_1  navigate_to(floor.n.01_2)
agent_0  navigate_to(floor.n.01_2) -> unload_from(agent_1) -> place_on_top
agent_1 is a carrier by inference: it has no arm, so cargo on its back is the
only way it can move anything. agent_2, the drone, has a suction cup and is
not base-locked -- it is the alternative route, and the team has to choose.
Two teams, so chain and centralized have inter-team traffic to carry;
individual ignores the split.
Dice and Crazyflie are at scale 2.0 -- twice native -- by decision (user,
2026-09-12), and every later port keeps that: a 1.8 cm die and a 12 cm drone
were too small to see or to reason about at room scale. The drone's 2.0
replaces the 0.6 above; the dice's 2.0 is set in the sampler whitelist and
baked into the cached instance, so a re-sample is needed to change it.
